meta.title: Russian Honeypot: I Was Trained To Control A Man's Mind With Sex! | John Kiriakou & Aliia Roza
meta.speakers: John Kiriakou (former CIA officer), Aliia Roza (former Russian undercover agent); host Steven Bartlett
meta.thread_line: 5 threads · the alleged Jensen Huang honeypot · Nvidia fallout and a buy-the-dip call · how a honey trap is trained · the five-step manipulation playbook · life inside and after deep cover

snapshot: Former CIA officer John Kiriakou walks through press reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Wong, alleged by the guests to be a Chinese intelligence asset.
The alleged payoff: a $5 billion Nvidia chip order from **Megaspeed**, a 'Singapore' firm the New York Times found had two non-engineer staff and an empty Malaysian office.
Kiriakou says a CIA memo reached the president in early April 2026, yet Jensen still flew to China on Air Force One.
Both guests say Nvidia survives; Aliia Roza says she would buy the stock 'as much as I could' after a ~20% drop.
Roza, trained from 18 in a secret Russian program, lays out the honey-trap playbook: research, love bombing, information control, emotional dependency, isolation, gaslighting.
Her story: an 8-month undercover relationship with a crime boss, betrayal by a corrupt commander, a near-execution and the boss's later killing.
Kiriakou: about 90% of recruited assets do it for money; the FBI estimates 10,000-15,000 foreign intelligence officers in Washington.

themes.status: AS REPORTED BY NYT AND CNN, PER THE GUESTS
themes.title: The alleged honeypot that moved $5 billion of Nvidia chips to China
themes.lead: Kiriakou calls it a classic, low-sophistication operation: an attractive operative, a front company and a CEO who waved the order through.
bullets: Alice Wong claimed anchor jobs at Hunan TV and CCTV; Hunan TV says it never heard of her and no CCTV footage exists.
In 2023 she became managing director at **Megaspeed**, which bought $5 billion of chips with US approval and sent them to China; reports say chips sat unopened in Singapore.
Timeline cited: photographed together June 2024, in Taiwan May 2025, investigated October 2025; Jensen has been married 41 years.

Kiriakou: no due diligence because the orders came from the CEO — 'If Jensen Wong says go ahead and do this' — and 'bad tradecraft', since a real cover company is backstopped with an office, website and board.

Her husband Kangwi, a Chinese fund executive who founded Hexi Investment Management and faced Chinese stock-manipulation sanctions, has reportedly known Jensen since 2010 and introduced them; she joined his firm around 2015.
A CIA memo written March 2026 reached the president early April 2026; Marco Rubio blocked Jensen from the China trip, but Trump had him fly to Anchorage and sit beside Xi.
Bigger risk than chips, Kiriakou says: pillow talk about the president, DARPA and NSA — 'so far nobody's really talking about that.'

themes.title: Nvidia's fallout: board probe, FBI and a divorce bill — but the guests would buy
themes.lead: Both guests say Nvidia outlasts the scandal because it is the one company with these GPUs.
bullets: Kiriakou lists three problems for Jensen: an outside board investigation, an FBI probe tied to CIA/NSA/Pentagon, and no prenup.
Steven Bartlett cites reports the divorce could cost about $100 billion, with Jensen owning roughly 3% of Nvidia.
Shares fell **about 20%** after the affair went public three weeks earlier; Nvidia reports results on November 17.
Governance gap: 60 direct reports, a flat structure and no named successor; no one is calling for his resignation.
Roza: Nvidia spends about $10 million a year on Jensen's security, yet no background check flagged the relationship.
Roza floats that Kangwi could be the one buying shares cheaply now.

quote.text: with Jensen or without Jensen the Nvidia will become even more powerful and stronger and profitable.

themes.title: How Russia trained a honey trap — and paid $100 a month
themes.lead: Roza was handpicked at 18 into a secret KGB-derived program where 70-80% of the training was male psychology.
bullets: Her father, a high-ranking officer, steered her from design school into a criminal-investigation unit fighting human and drug trafficking.
Of about 350 first-year students, five girls were picked: set height, under 26, deliberately different looks (her nickname was 'exotic').
Salary was about $100 a month for six-day weeks; Kiriakou recalls Time magazine putting Russian diplomats at $100 a month — one's wife taught ice skating to feed them.
Arousal 'anchoring': train the brain to like the target via the target's photo, a perfume and a keyword, then reuse the anchor before meeting.

Social engineering on a crime boss called Vladimir: hired actor couples staged his lost love story over two months, then eight months as his girlfriend, bugging his house and passing notes via dead drops.
A corrupt commander outed her to install his own protégé; she was beaten, taken to a forest to be killed, talked her way out with Vladimir, and he was killed two months later.
She says two teammates died and that she opened doors for 'cleaning' teams; she carries guilt and attempted suicide.

quote.text: If I would compare my life to James Bond movie, I would be the one who would seduce James Bond

themes.watch: Personal account, not independently detailed on air; she declined to say whether she met Vladimir Putin, citing family still in Russia and people watching her.

themes.title: The five-brick manipulation playbook, and the red flags to spot it
themes.lead: Research, love bombing, information control, emotional dependency, isolation and gaslighting — the same steps Roza now teaches women to recognise.
bullets: Love bombing targets achievements, not looks; she greeted Kiriakou in Greek after learning his background, then asked a small favor so he would invest in her.
Information control maps the inner circle; isolation plants subtle doubts about whoever has an opinion on the relationship, so cutting them off feels like his idea.
Gaslighting makes the target doubt himself; she demonstrated it live on Kiriakou over a past interview quote.
Red flags: instant **mirroring** (test it by changing gesture), endless 'me too' similarities, and early 'we're soulmates' talk.
Body language: open posture, no bag on the lap, the eye-contact 'triangle', showing wrist and neck.
The 'milk technique': free association reveals whether to play the mother or the lover archetype.
Kiriakou: CIA trainers taught body language; old officers' war stories became a class he later mined by classified email.

quote.text: seduction, the art of seduction, it's not about loving someone. It's about what do we experience?

themes.status: KIRIAKOU OUT OF THE CIA SINCE 2004
themes.title: Why people spy, how deep cover works, and what it does to you
themes.lead: Kiriakou says money drives about 90% of recruits, then ideology, excitement, revenge or legacy.
bullets: The FBI estimates 10,000-15,000 foreign intelligence officers in Washington; Russia, France, Israel and China still run honey traps, the CIA largely stopped after the 1970s.
Best sources are overlooked insiders, like the White House valet; a DIA colleague built a career on a San Francisco cab driver.
NOC (non-official cover) officers live a cover job for 20-30 years; US companies routinely agree to host them.
Sleeper agents: an Arlington elementary teacher arrested; Jack Barsky walked into the FBI rather than answer his activation.
China once had poor English and was not a big threat; it has grown far more sophisticated over 20-30 years and can afford to try many operatives at once.
The CIA rarely runs decade-long operations 'because you can't get promoted that way'.
Both guests relate to sociopathic traits; Roza says she has never been in love and keeps scanning rooms, as Kiriakou still checks his mirrors.

quote.text: I've said many, many times the CIA actively seeks to hire people with sociopathic tendencies.

takeaways.title: Separate CEO scandal from franchise value — check whether the moat depends on the person.
Watch key-person risk: 60 direct reports and no successor is a board problem, scandal or not.
Verify counterparties are backstopped — office, staff, website, board — before big orders.
Test fast rapport: change a gesture and see if it's copied, and be wary of instant 'soulmate' talk.
Use anchoring for good — a word, scent or breath routine to steady nerves before a talk.

other_news.title: Sources referenced: New York Times and CNN reporting, Time magazine, Kiriakou's own podcast, Neil Strauss's podcast To Die For, Jack Barsky's book, The Sopranos and LA Confidential as analogies, and Roza's book *Honey Trap: How Never Be Trapped Again*.

Kiriakou recalls Colin Powell asking who would run a plot to kill George H.W. Bush; 47 cruise missiles hit Iraqi intelligence HQ at night and killed a janitor — 'Powell killed the janitor,' his boss said.
After prison, Kiriakou says the FBI tailed him routinely; he once bought the surveillance team pizza, and Aldrich Ames and Robert Hanssen were caught through Western penetrations of the KGB.
Roza's stated goal: buy an island and build an internet-free orphanage for thousands of children.

glossary.def: An operation using a seductive operative to gain access, information or favors from a well-connected target.
Making a cover identity checkable: real office, phone, website, records.
Non-official cover: an intelligence officer posing in a private job rather than at an embassy.
An operative placed to live a normal life until activated.
A hidden spot for passing notes or material without meeting.
Handing an asset to a successor case officer in person.
